**Ways tested: 7,848. Ways passing (300 or more filled orders and profit in both halves): 100. Ways on forward paper: 88. New ways this week (from 16 Nov): 3881 from traders' methods (a), 3385 from our own data (b), 977 from other ideas (c).**

Every row went through the same test: real prices on offer with the money shown there (at least £2), offers filled only by later trades that went through the price and only for the money that traded, £50 a bet and £50 lay liability at most, 2% commission on each market's net winnings, an exit that could not fill held to the result, stale quotes not used. £ a month = the money made over all the days of data the way could have traded, times 30.4. Halves are by date. Paper only: nothing here is real money.

Sources: a = how proven exchange traders are documented to earn; b = what our own recorded data shows (history-file slices enter only as ideas and are tested here at real prices); c = anything else. Rows can overlap: several ways may be the same bets described differently (for example laying football selections priced at a 20-30% chance before the start, which is mostly laying the draw). Do not add their £ a month together; a passing way is only proven once its forward paper passes the gate.

The 'Way' column is the way's number in the registry; 'same bets as way N' means the row shares 90% or more of its orders (market, selection, side) with way N and is the same effect.
